messages:
maria: Heads-up — in the sampleapp streaming demo I just repro'd a weird interleave when the client reconnects fast. Happens in node SDK 1.3.2 and the local sample server.

maria: Repro steps: start stream, ctrl-c immediately, restart client within ~200ms. Sometimes you get a merged JSON where the last line of previous event joins the first line of the new event. :confused:

maria: Example (raw SSE capture):
```
event: message
id: 42
data: {"chunk": "part1"}

event: message
id: 43
data: {"chunk": "part2"}

# after reconnect we sometimes see:
event: message
id: 43
data: {"chunk": "part2"}
data: {"chunk": "part3"}
```

sam: can you paste the client logs? is it the browser client or node sample?

maria: node sampleapp (devex/sample-stream v0.9). client log snapshot: `sse-parser: got fragment (len=48), got fragment (len=21) -> assembled as single data event`.

li: odd. sounds like fragment reassembly bug in the client parser. do we flush last event on abort? which keepalive/heartbeat is configured on that sample?

maria: default sample uses 60s heartbeat, but reconnect is immediate. not a heartbeat issue imo — looks like partial buffer wasn't cleared on abort.

diego: I suspect two races: (1) client abort leaves partial chunk in parser buffer, (2) reconnect sets up new socket and the new initial bytes get appended before the parser noticed EOF, so they collapse into one `data` payload. parser should detect client disconnect and force-emit/clear partial chunk or treat missing delimiter as start of new event.

sam: can we reproduce with curl? if reproducible we can add an integration test.

maria: yes repro with curl, command I used:
```bash
# terminal A
python -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 8080  # sample backend (simulated)
# terminal B - start client
curl -N http://localhost:8080/stream
# ctrl-c then quickly run again -> sometimes merged chunks
```

li: thanks. two quick mitigation ideas: (A) ignore leading `data:` lines that arrive without preceding blank line (i.e., treat them as start-of-event), (B) on client socket `close`/`error` force reset parser buffer. both are cheap.

diego: agreed. short-term do (B) in node sdk: on `req.on('close')` call `parser.reset()` and set a 1ms drain window before accepting new socket data. long-term add sequence ids and reassembly based on `id:` header if present.

sam: small patch suggestion for parser.js (node sdk) — please review: 
```js
// on incoming chunk processing
if (line === '' && parser.buffer === '') continue; // skip stray blank lines
if (socket.closed) parser.reset();
// assemble normally
```

sam: also add test that simulates abrupt close + immediate new connection to catch regressions.

maria: implemented the reset-on-close hack in my local branch and the repro stopped happening consistently. will open PR. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: Created issue DE-1129: "node-sdk: parser buffer not cleared on client reconnect -> merged data events" (link: https://tracker.internal/DE-1129)

maria: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/789 — includes unit test and a comment explaining the race. requesting review from @sam @li.

li: nice. if accepted let's backport to 1.3.x release and update sampleapp. also add a small note in streaming docs about immediate reconnect edge-case.

sam: will review today. if green I'll merge and hand to releng for backport. thanks for the quick triage. :eyes:

maria: thanks all — saved a demo for a partner this afternoon, so this was high priority. follow-up: I'll also run fuzzing for random reconnect intervals to be safe.
